readingMode: All 20 PDF pages sequentially read, including both index pages, campaign introduction and all 59 measures. Original pages 7-9 visually inspected for population/toll conditions. Display whitespace collapsed only; cached text and offsets unchanged.

coverage.authoredAnalysis: Cover explicitly names the general election of 23 July 2023; no position inferred from branding.
Index, first six sections: territorial cohesion, transport, healthcare, education/science, industry/tourism and heritage; all numbered measures read below.
Index, remaining six sections: environment, equality, rural economy, work, security and transversal policy; 59 measures in total.
Congress/Senate campaign introduction explicitly addresses Ávila voters. Infrastructure neglect and representative-performance claims are attributed rhetoric, not independently established facts.
Campaign questions and historical territorial inequality argument. These voter-facing rhetorical prompts are not quiz wording or factual proof of consequences.

Measures 1-3: State budget investment for province/capital, balanced territorial development, rural population retention through transport, telecoms, entrepreneurship, health/education/social/cultural access. No exact spending allocation.

Completes rural services; measures 4-7: high-speed internet/TV, income-tax reduction in municipalities below 10,000 people and depopulation relief linked to service/transport travel times; public agency decentralisation and technical/economic municipal grant support.

Measures 8-10: include Ávila in Atlantic corridor beyond freight, passenger/freight rail and Madrid commuter network, better travel times/frequencies/stations. AP-51/AP-6/AP-61 concession end proposed for 2024 rather than 2029; original rendering inspected.

Completes toll measure: discounts up to 80% for registered Ávila city/province residents who habitually use tolls. Measures 11-14: A-40/N-110 projects and State road safety, regular/on-demand rural buses and concession compliance. Not universal free motorway.

Measures 15-17: healthcare/pharmacy rights across regions, independent management reform for chronic illness/staffing, access to neighbouring-region healthcare by proximity for peripheral Ávila areas; no specified treatment basket or privatisation decision.

Measures 18-21: stable education pact/equity, educational community priority, education/science/technology spending toward European average and university research/labour relevance/international experience. Spending denominator/timeframe unspecified.

Measures 22-25: local firm quality/innovation/jobs/cooperatives and rural development; self-employed law for retirement/sickness/unemployment protection, business succession and collaborative entrepreneurship; industrial investment/estate modernisation begins.

Completes industrial estates with telecom/electricity/transport. Measures 26-29: sustainable tourism including dark skies, cultural/nature/religious/language/events tourism, heritage collaboration and national-museum exhibitions; no funding amounts.

Measures 30-34: national wildfire prevention framework, Puerto del Pico BRIF category A expansion, emergency military unit in Ávila, carbon-sink forest-management studies and reservoir/drought investments. Carbon-income promise is a source claim.

Completes water investment; measures 35-38: Burguillo localities water priority during shortages and irrigation rights dialogue, river maintenance agreements, nondiscrimination within Constitution/law and residence-independent opportunities. Equality discussion continues.

Completes rural/peripheral public-service equity. Measures 39-41: gender pay-gap initiatives and work/family reconciliation, digital inclusion for vulnerable/older/poor/isolated people, rural farm/livestock/entrepreneur support; no quantified leave or wage rule.

Measures 42-45: adequate non-abusive agricultural insurance, protect extensive livestock against wolves through research/technology/traditional measures/compensation and management plan, food industry aid, decent jobs/telework/flexibility and rural services. No explicit wolf delisting/culling policy.

Measures 46-49: State worker reskilling, sufficient citizen-service staffing, accessible appointment requests including in-person channels, fill State posts in province and public employment by workload; modernise National Police School.

Measures 50-56: official police degrees, pay parity among regional police/Guardia Civil/Policía Nacional; Spanish territorial unity, residence-independent rights/State jobs, Spanish as vehicular school language and official State language, poverty/social exclusion action. No exact regional-language exclusion.

Measures 57-59: dignified sustainable pensions within Toledo pact, older/isolated/vulnerable people and children support, loneliness policies. No exact pension indexation/age mechanism or additional annex.
